Salmon spawn in freshwater rivers, returning to the natal rivers where they were born [d2][d4][d6]. In the Pacific Northwest and Alaska, Pacific salmon species spawn in rivers such as the Columbia River, Snake River, Chilkat River, Chitina River, Copper River, Coos River, and Coquille River, among others [d1][d3][d5][d8][d9]. Specifically, ocean-type chinook spawn in large rivers like the main stem of the Columbia or Snake rivers, while chum salmon spawn in the lower reaches of the Columbia mainstem [d3][d9]. Atlantic salmon spawn in rivers as well — U.S. Atlantic salmon are found in a handful of rivers in Maine, and Atlantic salmon also spawn in Irish rivers from November to January [d6][d7].
